_meta.what_this_is: The segments a harness assembles into a prompt, each with a token count and whether it is STABLE (identical from request to request) or VOLATILE (changes every request, like a timestamp or per-request id). A model prompt cache reuses the longest leading run of tokens identical to the previous request and only reprocesses the rest. So the ORDER of the segments decides the cache: put a volatile segment first and the cache breaks immediately (reprocess everything); keep all the stable segments first and the cache covers them, leaving only the small volatile tail to reprocess.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The segment sizes and stable flags are hand-authored so a bad ordering (volatile first) caches 0 tokens and reprocesses all 1820, while a good ordering (volatile last) caches 1800 and reprocesses only 20. Every cached/processed count is computed in prefix.py.
_meta.format: segments: {name: {tokens, stable}}; layouts: {name: [segment names in order]}.
